key_insight: Centered finite-volume transport with explicit pressure relaxation nearly preserves kinetic energy in weakly compressible single- and two-phase turbulence, while harmonic face densities improve phase-mass positivity.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a low-dissipation foundation for multiphase large-eddy simulation, with a local pressure algorithm suited to future GPU and adaptive-mesh implementations.
method: Couple kinetic-energy-preserving centered advection with conservative diffuse-interface regularization.
Use harmonic face densities to connect phase-volume and phase-mass transport.
Apply pressure-increment relaxation with compatible cell and face operators on collocated grids.
evidence_signal: In inviscid turbulence on 128³ cells at t*=8, relative kinetic-energy changes stayed below 1.2×10⁻⁷ in magnitude for single-phase and density-ratio-1000 two-phase cases; matched upwind runs retained only 3.60% and 30.72% of initial energy, respectively.
watch_item: Positivity and pressure-iteration energy estimates are conditional; GPU and adaptive-mesh scalability remain future work rather than demonstrated results.
paper_title: A centered finite-volume method with explicit pressure relaxation for weakly compressible single- and two-phase flows
